value.title: Cross-model review r2 (final) — statusline-generation-badge
value.note:
SUBJECT: branch 129-statusline-generation-badge at 95220ec4. The whole delta since the r1 subject (fc01d0e6) is 4 fix hunks, the r1 record, and the reviewer-seat stamp — 9 files, +157/-8. I diffed the full range rather than the named fixes, because a re-review's job is partly to check that nothing else rode along. Nothing did, with one unannounced line noted as n2.

METHOD: every fix re-derived rather than accepted. For f1 I re-ran the exact r1 repro on the same real dual-present pane. For f3 I did not settle for the new test being green — I replicated its harness by hand and ran the NEW fake against the OLD script, to prove the witness is red before the fix rather than green from birth.

VERDICT: APPROVE. f1, f2, f3, f4 all fixed. n1 stays deferred to prime as agreed; two new NITs recorded (n2, n3), neither blocking, both one line.

AC FINAL
- AC1 TRUE — the r1 counterexample is gone. Same pane %3060, same stdin, contradicting PIJ_SESSION_ID still exported: now renders `rs ⛓ pij-relative-cheetah`, byte-identical to the env-unset control. This is the same command that produced `legacy ⛓ pij-quarrelsome-caribou` in r1.
- AC2 TRUE — re-verified after the fix, both halves: rs miss with legacy present renders the dim legacy tag and its id; a pane in neither store renders no pij segment, keeps every other segment, exit 0. I also confirmed the empty-segment output on an unowned pane is IDENTICAL before and after the fix, so the `unset` did not quietly change the fallback path.
- AC3 TRUE — unchanged since r1. Code and unit tests on both generations and both surfaces, verified by me (25/25 across the two vitest files). The live-omp-footer half still rests on the author's capture; I did not start a real omp in either round and I am not going to imply otherwise.
- AC4 TRUE — against the bar the plan now states. AC4's text carries the ruled ≤100ms and ≥10x and names the ruling that superseded 50ms. Author median 92.10ms at 28.52x; my own median 67.98ms. Both clear it.
- AC5 TRUE — unchanged and re-run: 4/4 statusline_ tests watched, including the now-stronger rs-first case.

WHAT THE FIXES ARE WORTH, beyond being correct:
- f1's shape is right. `$(unset PIJ_SESSION_ID; ...)` scopes the unset to the command-substitution subshell, so the legacy branch at :90 still sees the variable it needs. I checked that rather than assuming it: `pij whoami` under the same env still resolves the legacy id, and the unowned-pane output is unchanged from the pre-fix script.
- f3 is the fix I care most about, because it is the one that makes f1 unable to recur. A fake that can only succeed cannot witness a resolution order; this one now refuses on an inherited id, which is the actual production behaviour it was standing in for.

value.finding:
FIXED. harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh:78 now reads:

  RS_OUTPUT=$(unset PIJ_SESSION_ID; "$PIJ_RS_BIN" --json whoami --pane "$TMUX_PANE" 2>/dev/null)

RE-DERIVED, not accepted — the r1 repro rerun verbatim on the same pane. %3060 is still genuinely dual-present (pid 87487 under pij-quarrelsome-caribou in the legacy store and under pij-relative-cheetah in rs).

  env PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-quarrelsome-caribou TMUX_PANE=%3060 sh harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh
    r1: ESC[2mlegacyESC[0m ESC[34m⛓ pij-quarrelsome-caribouESC[0m
    r2: ESC[33mrsESC[0m   ESC[34m⛓ pij-relative-cheetahESC[0m
  env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID TMUX_PANE=%3060 (control):
    r2: ESC[33mrsESC[0m   ESC[34m⛓ pij-relative-cheetahESC[0m   — byte-identical to the line above

The two env states now produce the same output, which is the property AC1 needs: the pane decides, not the inherited assertion.

I CHECKED THE OBVIOUS WAY THIS FIX COULD HAVE OVERSHOT, since `unset` on a variable the next branch depends on is exactly the kind of fix that trades one bug for another. The unset is inside a command substitution, so POSIX scopes it to that subshell and the legacy branch at :90 is unaffected. Verified rather than reasoned: `PIJ_DAEMON_GENERATION=legacy pij whoami` under the same environment still resolves pij-quarrelsome-caribou, and the rendered output for an unowned pane (%99999, where rs misses and legacy declines) is identical between the pre-fix script at fc01d0e6 and the fixed script — no segment gained, none lost.

shellcheck -s sh: clean.
value.receipt: r1 repro rerun verbatim on pane %3060 with contradicting PIJ_SESSION_ID and with env -u, outputs compared; pre-fix script recovered at fc01d0e6 and run on an unowned pane for the non-leak comparison; `pij whoami` under the same env re-checked; shellcheck -s sh clean

value.finding:
FIXED. plan.dd.json AC4 now reads "median wall time over 10 warm runs with rs answering ≤ 100ms and at least 10× faster than the forced legacy tsx path ... Prime ruling 2026-09-02 supersedes the original 50ms target", and plan.dd.md is rebuilt to match.

This is the right shape of amendment, and worth naming as such: the superseded number is GONE from the AC row rather than sitting beneath a newer ruling, and the row says whose ruling replaced it and when. A reader who finds this row in six months does not have to go and find the receipt to learn which bar was real. Both halves of my finding are addressed — the bar matches the evidence, and the change is attributed.

Evidence against the new bar, mine and the author's: my median 67.98ms (54.0-90.4, host load 67.22); the author's 92.10ms with 28.52x over the forced tsx path. Both inside ≤100ms and ≥10x.

Residual, not a reopening: see n2 — G4 still carries the old ~50ms figure.
value.receipt: AC4 text read from plan.dd.json and the rebuilt plan.dd.md; repo-wide grep for the 50ms figure across the plan folder (only G4 remains, recorded as n2); own 10-run timing median 67.98ms at host load 67.22

value.finding:
FIXED, AND THE WITNESS IS PROVEN RED ON THE PRE-FIX TREE. The fake rs at claude_settings.rs:1590-1598 now refuses with `{"ok":false,"error":"refused"}` and exit 2 whenever PIJ_SESSION_ID is set, and the runner at :1629 sets PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-other-seat for every invocation.

A green test is not evidence that it would have caught anything, so I did not stop at `cargo test ... 4 passed`. I replicated the test's harness by hand — same two fakes, same PATH/HOME/TMUX_PANE/PIJ_SESSION_ID/LEGACY_MARKER environment, same captured-shape stdin — and ran it against BOTH scripts:

  old (fc01d0e6)  -> dim `legacy` tag, id=pij-legacy-seat, legacy fake INVOKED (marker written)
  new (95220ec4)  -> yellow `rs` tag,  id=pij-rs-seat,     legacy fake NOT invoked

Against the pre-fix script this test fails on two of its own assertions — the `\u{1b}[33mrs\u{1b}[0m ... pij-rs-seat` match, and `assert!(!legacy_marker.exists())`. So it is a witness, not a test that was born green.

`cargo test -p pij-harnesses statusline_`: 4 passed, watched.
value.receipt: new fake and runner env read at :1590-1598 and :1629; test harness replicated by hand and run against both fc01d0e6 and 95220ec4 — legacy marker written by the old script, not by the new; `cargo test -p pij-harnesses statusline_` 4 passed, watched

value.finding:
FIXED. index.test.ts:287 now asserts `expect(sessionNames.at(-1)).toMatch(/^legacy·pij-/)` on the reasserted name, so the reassertion path no longer passes on a count alone.

The legacy spelling is correct for that test, not a slip — that case runs the FsRegistry arm, which is why `/^legacy·/` is what passes there. Composed with session-name.test.ts:197 (which witnesses that the generation argument is what produces the prefix), this makes `publication.daemonGeneration` load-bearing: hardcode the wrong constant at index.ts:555 and this assertion fails.

Residual, not a reopening: see n3 — the rs arm of the reassertion path still has no assertion of its own.

index.test.ts 17/17 and session-name.test.ts 8/8, watched (25/25 in one run).
value.receipt: index.test.ts:276-292 read in full; session-name.test.ts:197 cross-checked for the generation-to-prefix link; vitest 25/25 across both files, watched

value.finding:
NIT — UNATTRIBUTED LINE IN THE FIX DIFF. plan.dd.json lost `"references": []` in the same commit that amended AC4, and no message mentioned it. It is almost certainly a `ddocs build` normalisation of an empty array and it changes nothing. I raise it only because a change with no stated reason is worse than un-auditable: the next person to read this diff has to invent a cause for it, and the cheapest available story is "something is wrong with the tooling". One clause in the commit message would have cost nothing.

Second half of the same nit, and the more useful one: G4 in plan.dd.json:26 and plan.dd.md:39 still says "must not exceed ~50ms when rs answers". AC4 now supersedes it explicitly, so a careful reader reconciles — but the goal and the acceptance criterion for the same property now state different numbers, which is the exact condition f2 was about, moved one row up. Smallest fix: amend G4's text to ~100ms with the same superseding clause, and rebuild.
value.receipt: git diff fc01d0e6..HEAD over the whole tree, not just the named fixes; grep for 50ms across the plan folder

value.finding: NIT — the reassertion witness covers one arm. index.test.ts now asserts the generation prefix on the legacy reassertion; the rs reassertion still has no content assertion of its own. The risk is small because both arms flow through the same `publication.daemonGeneration` field and one closure, so a mutation that breaks rs almost certainly breaks legacy too. But "almost certainly" is what the unchanged arm always looks like right up until someone special-cases it. If a second assertion is cheap in the rs-arm test, it is worth one line; if it is not, this is fine as it stands.
value.receipt: index.ts:552-556 read; both reassertion call sites traced to the single publication.daemonGeneration field

value.finding: CARRIED FORWARD FROM r1, unchanged and still deferred to prime by agreement. `backup_statusline_script` returns Ok and silently takes no backup for a `~/`-command when home.parent() is not the real $HOME, for a relative command, and for a command with an interpreter prefix. Bounded — the prior script is dereferenced, never deleted — and it demonstrably works for both spellings that occur in practice. Restated here only so it is inherited as a list item rather than rediscovered by whoever reviews the next installer change.

value.rationale: The r1 counterexample reruns clean on the same real dual-present pane, and the two env states now agree byte for byte. I checked the fix's blast radius rather than only its effect: the unset is subshell-scoped, the legacy branch still resolves, and the unowned-pane output is unchanged from the pre-fix script.

Amended by excision and attributed to the ruling that superseded it — the 50ms figure is gone from the AC row rather than layered under a newer one. G4 still carries the old number; that is recorded as n2 rather than reopening this.

The strongest of the four. The fake now refuses on an inherited id, and I proved the test is red on the pre-fix tree by running its harness against the old script — it fails two assertions there. This is what stops f1 recurring silently; the fix to the script alone would not have.

The reassertion path now asserts content, not just a count, and the legacy spelling is the correct one for that arm. Composed with the publisher test, publication.daemonGeneration is load-bearing. The rs arm remains unwitnessed — n3, one line, not blocking.
Two one-line record cleanups: attribute the dropped references key, and bring G4's ~50ms into line with the ruled AC4. Neither affects behaviour; both affect what the next reader believes.
Small and honest to leave. Both arms share one field and one closure, so the legacy assertion covers the realistic mutations; the unchanged arm is worth one line only if it is cheap.
Prime's call, unchanged from r1 and explicitly out of this plan's scope.
